subject: Tenant BYOK: key derivation proofs + rotation telemetry for SOC 2 review
messages:
From: Amy Chen <security@acme-corp.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: 2027-05-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: BYOK derivation and rotation telemetry for SOC 2

Hi Jasmine,

We're starting our SOC 2 fieldwork next week and need a focused package showing how Redwood handles tenant BYOK (bring-your-own-key) for Acme. Specifically looking for:
- KDF/DERIVATION algorithm used to derive envelope keys (test vectors welcome)
- Evidence that KEKs are never exported in plaintext (attestation or logs)
- Signed rotation commits (who initiated, epoch timestamps) for April-May 2027
- Transport telemetry showing TLS mutual-auth for key-transfer operations (sample trace acceptable)

Can you provide a zip with the artifacts or point me to a secure drive link? The audit will want both the spec-level docs and example telemetry/logs.

Thanks,
Amy Chen
Security Engineer, Acme Corp
security@acme-corp.com

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Chen <security@acme-corp.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-22T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: BYOK derivation and rotation telemetry for SOC 2

Hi Amy — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to provide a focused package for Acme. High level: Redwood uses per-tenant envelope keys derived from the tenant's master key via HKDF-SHA256 with explicit context strings (tenant-id, model-region, purpose=envelope). KEKs (key-encryption keys) are generated inside an FIPS-validated HSM and never leave the HSM plaintext.

I'll coordinate artifacts: spec (KDF text + test vectors), a signed HSM attestation PDF, rotation commit logs (April-May), and a sampled transport telemetry file (anonymized traces showing mutual TLS and client cert validation).

I'll have the initial bundle ready by EOD PST and upload to a secure Drive folder; we'll share Docs and a short readme explaining how to interpret the rotation CSV. Irene will attach the HSM attestation and Neha will include the log extracts.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, Amy Chen <security@acme-corp.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-22T12:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: BYOK derivation and rotation telemetry for SOC 2

Amy / Jasmine — attaching the formal artifacts we typically provide for SOC 2:

Attachments included in the Drive link: 
- hsm_fips140-2-attestation-serial-3947.pdf (vendor-signed attestation showing HSM model, FIPS validation level, and certificate chain).
- kdf-spec-and-test-vectors-20270522.txt (plain-text spec of HKDF usage, salt/label conventions, and three test vectors derived from a sample tenant master key).
- rotation-commit-log-202704-202705.csv (sanitized CSV: epoch, rotation_id, initiated_by, signature, previous_digest).
- transport-telemetry-sample-202705.json (anonymized JSON traces showing TLS handshake events and mutual-cert verification during key wrapping/unwrapping flows).

Quick notes:
1) KDF: We use HKDF-SHA256 with a 32-byte salt derived from the tenant-id; context string = "redwood:envelope:v1". Test vectors in the text file map to the derived envelope key bytes so the auditor can reproduce derivation.
2) HSM/KEK handling: KEKs are resident-only; any wrapping operations happen inside the HSM. The attestation contains the HSM serial, firmware version, and the provider signature.
3) Rotation commits: Each commit is signed with a rotation authority key; the CSV includes the signature field. The auditor can request the public rotation authority key (we include its fingerprint in the readme).
4) Transport: Telemetry is sampled at 0.5% rate for key ops to limit PII; included sample demonstrates client cert validation and TLS 1.3 with mutual auth.

Drive link (access granted to acme-corp domain): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B_example_redwood_evidence
DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/3aBc-rotation-playbook-sign (playbook acceptance for emergency rotation access)

If the auditor needs the public rotation authority key or wants an interactive session to validate test vectors, we can schedule a short call.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Manager, Applied Cryptography — Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Chen <security@acme-corp.com>, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-22T14:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: BYOK derivation and rotation telemetry for SOC 2

On 2027-05-22 09:12 AM Amy Chen wrote:
> We're starting our SOC 2 fieldwork next week and need a focused package showing how Redwood handles tenant BYOK...
> Can you provide a zip with the artifacts or point me to a secure drive link?

Thanks — I uploaded the full archive (sanitized) to the Drive folder referenced below. For quick reference I've pasted small snippets here from the rotation CSV and a transport trace (anonymized):

--- rotation-commit-log-202704-202705.csv (sample row) ---
epoch_utc,rotation_id,initiated_by,signature_hex,prev_digest
2027-04-25T02:14:08Z,rot-20270425-7f3a,Jenkins:rotation-job,9f4c2b7a...a5f1,3d2b9c8f...b1

Notes: signature_hex is a hex-encoded ECDSA signature over the commit payload (rotation_id + epoch + prev_digest). The auditor can verify using the rotation authority public key fingerprint: SHA256:AbCdEf1234567890examplefingerprint

--- transport-telemetry-sample-202705.json (excerpt) ---
{
  "trace_id": "t-5b9f",
  "events": [
    {"ts": "2027-05-14T18:04:12Z", "event": "tls_client_hello", "tls_version": "1.3", "client_cert_present": true},
    {"ts": "2027-05-14T18:04:12Z", "event": "tls_server_certificate_verified", "server_cert_chain_ok": true},
    {"ts": "2027-05-14T18:04:13Z", "event": "key_wrap_request", "status": "ok"}
  ]
}

Per Acme domain policy we granted drive access to the acme-corp group. If the auditor requires raw syslog exports (longer retention) we can coordinate a time-bound read-only S3 bucket share with short-lived credentials and an access justification ticket.

Let me know if you want a walkthrough with the auditor on reproducing KDF vectors.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
